name: L Visa (tourism) / unilateral visa-free entry

requirements.blocker_text: China's unilateral visa-free policy, extended through 31 December 2026, covers ordinary-passport holders from a growing list of countries (roughly 45+ as of this research, including Australia, France, Germany, Italy, and Spain) for stays up to 30 days for tourism, business, family visits, or transit -- other nationalities need an L (tourist) or M (business) visa.
requirements.fix_path: Apply for an L visa at a Chinese embassy or consulate if not on the visa-free list.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires proof of tourism purpose -- a round-trip itinerary, hotel bookings, or an invitation letter from a host in China; does not authorise work or study.
requirements.fix_path: Apply for the relevant work or study route instead if the purpose is employment.

evidence_required.document: Passport valid at least 6 months with 2 blank pages
Itinerary, hotel bookings, or invitation letter

outcome.duration_length: L visa typically 30-90 days per stay; visa-free entry up to 30 days per stay
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: up to 30 days per visa-free stay; L visa duration varies by nationality and consular decision

sources.title: TravelChinaGuide -- China Visa: Chinese Visa Application, Types, E-arrival Card, describing the L/M/X/Z visa categories and the unilateral visa-free policy extended to 31 December 2026

notes: HONEST SOURCING GAP: China's National Immigration Administration (nia.gov.cn) is the genuine tier-1 authority and was successfully fetched elsewhere in this build (see cn_naturalisation), but its specific visa-category and visa-free-list pages were not isolated and fetched in this research pass -- this route rests on a well-established, widely cross-corroborated tier-3 travel-guide source rather than a direct nia.gov.cn or Ministry of Foreign Affairs fetch. Kept as published rather than draft because the core facts (visa categories, general visa-free mechanism, 30-day cap) are stable, long-standing, and consistent across every source checked, unlike the more volatile country-list specifics. Change of status to a long-term category from inside China while on L-visa or visa-free status is not permitted; applicants must leave and apply for the target visa from outside China, the same pattern seen across nearly every 'visit' category route in this dataset.
